How to Apply to the McWhirter Graduate Program in Chemical Engineering
Applications to the McWhirter Graduate Program in Chemical Engineering are accepted online only through the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School’s Online Application Portal.
Key dates for Ph.D. applicants: December 15 for early admission, January 8 for regular admission. However late applications will be considered if positions in the program remain available. Late applicants are encouraged to inform the associate head for Graduate Studies of their intent.
The program uses a holistic admission approach where candidates are assessed on the following:
Preparation in Chemical Engineering Fundamentals: The candidate should demonstrate prior academic performance that indicates that they will be successful in the graduate courses and that they have the academic background to perform research in chemical engineering. The candidate is advised to explain, when possible, any poor performance in core STEM classes in their Statement of Purpose.
Research Experience: Prior research experience in academic, national laboratory or industrial setting is preferred to demonstrate acumen and potential for independent research. Please include your research supervisor as one of the references if applicable. Other work experiences that demonstrate the ability to solve problems, work on deadlines, and work on a team are equally valuable to illustrate research potential.
Research Interest Alignment: Motivation for Ph.D. and topics of interest are clearly aligned with the faculty. The outstanding candidate will note how Penn State provides a unique fit to these interests and will identify several potential faculty advisors that align with their motivation and career goals.
Creativity and Independent Problem Solving: Creativity in problem solving is highly desired for graduate students. The outstanding candidate will provide specific example(s) of their independent contributions towards the solution of a significant problem.
Character and Integrity: Specific actions and situations that demonstrate the character and integrity of the candidate should be included in the Statement of Purpose. Leadership and volunteer activities are some examples that can illustrate character.
Drive and Resilience: Overcoming adversity and successful strategies to tackling difficult challenges are both attributes of successful graduate students.
Communication Skills: Both oral and written communication skills are needed to be successful as a graduate student. Activities and awards that illustrate communication excellence as well as a concise, easy to read Statement of Purpose can demonstrate these skills in the outstanding candidate.
The following items are required as part of the application process:
A transcript from all institutions attended, both undergraduate and graduate
An unofficial copy is sufficient for the review process; if you are recommended for admission by the Admissions Committee, you will be notified by the Fox Graduate School that official/original transcripts/documents and their official English translation must be sent from the originating institutions for review by the Fox Graduate School in order to finalize an admission decision. Notarized copies are not sufficient. This step is only required after the application has been reviewed and if the applicant is offered admission.
Current Penn State students do not need to upload transcripts.
Statement of Purpose (and résumé if desired)
Write a brief essay of why you want to study in the McWhirter Graduate Program in Chemical Engineering at Penn State and your area(s) of interest as well as your experiences in independent problem solving, leadership, persistence, and research. The Statement of Purpose should address the holistic admission criteria described above.
The McWhirter Graduate Program strives to build a chemical engineering community with diverse perspectives from all backgrounds and identities. Here you may describe any aspects that give a more complete picture of you and your capabilities, or any participation in activities that are aligned with the Penn State Values.
Three letters of recommendation
The references you list in the online application will be given directions for submitting their letters.
We will accept letters by mail in a sealed and signed envelope if your references choose not to submit their letters online.
Please ask your references to describe not only your academic and research skills but also your personal qualities relevant to graduate study.
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) – for international students
TOEFL/IELTS Institution code is 2660; Department code is 64
ALL international students from non-English speaking countries are required to submit a TOEFL or IELTS score.
A minimum score of 80 overall of the TOEFL iBT® is required.
A minimum score of 19 on the speaking section of the TOEFL iBT® is required.
A minimum of 6.5 is required for all sections of the IELTS exam.
EXCEPTION: International students who have obtained a degree from an accredited university in the United States are not required to submit the TOEFL or IELTS score.
Applicants who do not meet the minimum requirements will be considered for admission on a provisional basis and required to take English course(s).
PLEASE NOTE: All test scores (TOEFL/IELTS and GRE) should be sent to Penn State electronically from the testing agency.
Please do not submit information with your application that cannot be used in the admission decision process, e.g., Individual Education Plans (IEP), medical records, statement from physicians or psychologists, or legal documents. Such information will be destroyed and will not be included in the application packet.
Official report of Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores
GRE scores are not required.
Deadlines
The McWhirter Graduate Program in Chemical Engineering accepts graduate applications on a continuous, rolling basis. For preferable consideration for admission, the following deadlines apply:
Master of science (M.S.) degree applicants:
March 30 for fall admission
Reviewing of applications for the M.S. program will begin February 1 and continue on a rolling basis until April 15.
No application will be received for spring admission
Doctoral (Ph.D.) degree applicants:
December 15 for early admission
January 8 for regular admission
Notification
Ph.D. applications completed by the posted December deadline will be reviewed by the Admissions Committee and decisions will be informed during early January.
Ph.D. applications completed by the posted January deadline will be reviewed by the Admissions Committee and decisions will be informed during early February.
M.S. applications completed by the posted April deadline will be reviewed as early as mid-February and continuously on a rolling basis until all positions are filled. Acceptance letters will be emailed as reviews are completed.
When an application is approved by the Admissions Committee, the following will occur through different Penn State offices:
A letter of recommended acceptance will be sent to the admitted applicant by e-mail. The admission recommendation will be forwarded to the Fox Graduate School by the McWhirter Graduate Program of Chemical Engineering.
The Fox Graduate School must approve the McWhirter Graduate Program’s recommendation of acceptance. If approved, applicants will be notified by the Fox Graduate School.
International applicants will then be notified by the Directorate of International Student and Scholar Advising (DISSA), which will issue an I-20 form. Any questions regarding visas, I-20, etc., must be directed to the DISSA Office. The Waltemeyer Department of Chemical Engineering is unable to assist with international student visas.
All admitted applicants will be considered for research or teaching assistantships and applicable fellowships. Applicants will be notified by the McWhirter Graduate Program of any assistantship offers or fellowships at the time of admission.
PLEASE NOTE: The M.S. program requires that the student be able to provide self-support for the 30 credits for the duration of M.S. study (which is one year if there is no delay). Applicants seeking admission to this program will not be considered for financial supports from the Department or University.
The Admissions Committee carefully reviews each application and discusses the potential of each applicant. As such, the decisions of the Admissions Committee are final and not subject to further review.
